cases.sentence: Наташа, любимица молодых Мелюковых, с ними вместе исчезла в задние комнаты, куда была потребована пробка и ___ и мужские платья, которые в растворенную дверь принимали от лакея оголенные девичьи руки.
cases.explain: «разные халаты» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Natásha, the young Melyukóvs’ favorite, disappeared with them into the back rooms where a cork and various dressing gowns and male garments were called for and received from the footman by bare girlish arms from behind the door. Ten minutes later, all the young Melyukóvs joined the mummers.

cases.sentence: — говорила она, обращаясь к своей гувернантке и глядя в лицо своей дочери, представлявшей ___.
cases.explain: «казанского татарина» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “And who is this?” she asked her governess, peering into the face of her own daughter dressed up as a Kazán-Tartar. “I suppose it is one of the Rostóvs! Well, Mr. Hussar, and what regiment do you serve in?” she asked Natásha. “Here, hand some fruit jelly to the Turk!” she ordered the butler who was handing things round. “That’s not forbidden by his law.”

cases.sentence: После ___ и хороводов Пелагея Даниловна соединила всех дворовых и господ вместе, в один большой круг; принесли кольцо, веревочку и рублик, и устроились общие игры.
cases.explain: «русских плясок» — after the preposition «после», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: After Russian country dances and chorus dances, Pelagéya Danílovna made the serfs and gentry join in one large circle: a ring, a string, and a silver ruble were fetched and they all played games together.

cases.sentence: ___ и брови размазались по вспотевшим, разгоревшимся и веселым лицам.
cases.explain: «Пробочные усы» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: In an hour, all the costumes were crumpled and disordered. The corked eyebrows and mustaches were smeared over the perspiring, flushed, and merry faces. Pelagéya Danílovna began to recognize the mummers, admired their cleverly contrived costumes, and particularly how they suited the young ladies, and she thanked them all for having entertained her so well. The visitors were invited to supper in the drawing room, and the serfs had something served to them in the ballroom.

cases.sentence: — говорила за ужином ___, жившая у Мелюковых.
cases.explain: «старая девушка» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Now to tell one’s fortune in the empty bathhouse is frightening!” said an old maid who lived with the Melyukóvs, during supper.

cases.sentence: — Да вот так-то, пошла одна барышня, — сказала ___, — взяла петуха, два прибора — как следует, села.
cases.explain: «старая девушка» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Well,” began the old maid, “a young lady once went out, took a cock, laid the table for two, all properly, and sat down. After sitting a while, she suddenly hears someone coming … a sleigh drives up with harness bells; she hears him coming! He comes in, just in the shape of a man, like an officer—comes in and sits down to table with her.”

cases.sentence: Играли ли в колечко, в веревочку или рублик, разговаривали ли, как теперь, Николай не отходил от Сони и совсем ___ смотрел на нее.
cases.explain: «новыми глазами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Whether they were playing the ring and string game or the ruble game or talking as now, Nikoláy did not leave Sónya’s side, and gazed at her with quite new eyes. It seemed to him that it was only today, thanks to that burnt-cork mustache, that he had fully learned to know her. And really, that evening, Sónya was brighter, more animated, and prettier than Nikoláy had ever seen her before.

cases.sentence: Ему казалось, что он нынче только в ___, благодаря этим пробочным усам, вполне узнал ее.
cases.explain: «первый раз» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.

cases.sentence: Чего ждал до сих пор?» подумал Николай и, сбежав на крыльцо, он обошел угол дома по той тропинке, которая вела к ___.
cases.explain: «заднему крыльцу» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “I am a fool, a fool! what have I been waiting for?” thought Nikoláy, and running out from the porch he went round the corner of the house and along the path that led to the back porch. He knew Sónya would pass that way. Halfway lay some snow-covered piles of firewood and across and along them a network of shadows from the bare old lime trees fell on the snow and on the path. This path led to the barn. The log walls of the barn and its snow-covered roof, that looked as if hewn out of some precious stone, sparkled in the moonlight. A tree in the garden snapped with the frost, and then all was again perfectly silent. His bosom seemed to inhale not air but the strength of eternal youth and gladness.
